Each prompt is the text as he typed it; each window's text is the prompt's slice Pangram reports. Each check has the fields coverage.py reads (uuid, at as his history gives it, text_sha256 of the prompt, windows as [label, confidence, words, where]).

checks.prompt: I'm not advising lion's mane or ashwagandha, even though they're popular herbs for focus and stress, because some people report anhedonia (no joy or desire) and sexual dysfunction long after they stop taking them. Post-ashwa and post-lion's mane syndrome are rare, but we know about this phenomenon already from SSRIs and finasteride users, so if you're already on either herb, I'd quit it as soon as you notice any of that.

checks.prompt:
As you de-armor, you will feel naked and exposed, and you will assume everyone can see your anxiety, which they mostly can't. Nicholas Epley, Mindwise, calls this the "Illusion of Transparency."

On top of that, you'll tend to think people are judging you, when they're mostly just thinking about themselves, because your armored brain projects the threat it feels onto neutral faces. So during this protocol, do not trust your social intuition: assume you are misreading every room, at least until your heart rate is back down to your usual resting rate, and under 90 BPM, since a racing heart means your reasoning brain is offline (see the "Metabolic Red Line" below).
